hypothesis: In real sunflower capitula the two families of conspicuous parastichy spirals cross at a roughly constant angle along the radius of each head (isogonal), and that constant angle is seldom a right angle.
pass_criterion: Claim is supported if, among N>=30 heads with at least 3 measurable crossings in each of 3 radial bands (0.3-0.5R, 0.5-0.7R, 0.7-0.9R), BOTH hold: (a) in >=75% of heads the range of band-mean crossing angles is <=10 degrees (isogonal within tolerance); AND (b) <=25% of heads have an overall mean crossing angle within 90 +/- 5 degrees (orthogonal is infrequent).
fail_criterion: Claim is refuted if either (a) fewer than 50% of heads have a radial range of band-mean crossing angles <=10 degrees (angle not constant), or (b) more than 50% of heads have an overall mean crossing angle within 90 +/- 5 degrees (orthogonal intersection is common). Results between the pass and fail thresholds are reported as inconclusive.
interpretation: Thompson's 'spirals intersect isogonally' is read as: the angle between the two families of visible parastichy curves is constant along the radius, as for logarithmic spirals about a common pole. 'Orthogonal ... very infrequent' is read as: the crossing angle is rarely 90 degrees. Modern reinterpretation: real capitula follow Vogel/Fermat-type packing, not literal logarithmic spirals, so constancy is tested empirically with a 10-degree tolerance rather than exactly. Crossing angles are not recorded in the dataset; they must be measured by digitising the annotated parastichy lines in the deposited head images. The recorded parastichy counts identify the two families per head. Church's orthogonality claim is tested only through criterion (b).

dataset.name: Data from: Novel Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci structure in the sunflower: results of a citizen science experiment
dataset.publisher: Dryad Digital Repository (Swinton & Ochu, University of Manchester)
dataset.why_it_fits: The deposit contains 'Annotated seedhead images 20160205.zip' (sunflower head images with parastichies overlaid and counted) and count spreadsheets (MSF007_SunflowerData_20151020_anonymised.xlsx, JS annotations for MSF007_Countdata.xlsx). Fields used: the annotated images, to digitise parastichy line directions and compute crossing angles at several radii; and the parastichy counts and sample IDs, to identify the two families per head. It does not record angles directly, so they are measured by image analysis.
